title: Do the angles of a caved-in four sided shape add to 360 degrees?
description: A four sided shape has one corner that caves in, and the video asks if its four angles still add to three hundred sixty degrees. It joins the caved-in corner to the opposite corner, splits the shape into two triangles, and checks by drawing and measuring.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonal from the caved-in corner lies inside the shape, so it makes two triangles whose angles fill the four angles of the shape. Watch for students who think the rule fails because one angle is bigger than a straight angle.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 10)
video_script.why: The child cuts the caved-in shape into two triangles with a diagonal, as with a convex shape, and sees that the total of the four angles does not change.
video_script.substitution: Join the caved-in corner to the opposite corner so the diagonal lies inside, add the angles of the two triangles, and match them with the four angles of the shape.
video_script.anchor: quadrilateral ABCD whose corner D caves in, with the diagonal DB drawn inside it
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the angles of eigh B C D still add to three hundred sixty degrees

final_answer.value: Yes, the angle sum is still 360°
final_answer.spoken: yes, the angles of eigh B C D still add to three hundred sixty degrees

maths_rules: in ABCD the corner D caves in, so the diagonal DB lies inside the shape
DB splits ABCD into triangles ABD and CBD, each with angle sum 180 degrees
the angle of ABCD at D is angle ADB + angle BDC, and the angle at B is angle ABD + angle DBC
the angles at A and C belong to one triangle each
the six angles of the two triangles are exactly the four angles of ABCD, so the total is 180 + 180 = 360 degrees
check: draw such a shape, measure the four angles with a protractor and add them to get about 360
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonal from the caved-in corner lies inside, so two triangles fill the four angles and the total stays 360 degrees. The caved-in shape with its diagonal stays on the board.
